newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse seen rising after break.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse seen rising after break.

text.p: Stock brokers said on Wednesday they expected turnover on the Bucharest bourse to pick up when trading resumes on Thursday after a two-week break.
"Orders have accumulated in the meantime and turnover will rise, probably to around 75 million lei," one broker said.
The Bucharest bourse stayed closed for three consecutive sessions as it installed new software intended to improve trading and settlement.

"The new software provides more facilities, including the possibility to group more orders and thus trade a larger number of shares at a time. It will be helpful but it will not mean a dramatic rise in turnover because investor interest stays thin," said another broker.
He said investors were now waiting for seven companies which recently applied for a bourse listing to get a quotation and join in trading.
"The mood is one of waiting, investors are looking forward to the seven companies on the market, especially as some of them promise to be attractions," a trader said.
The seven companies include a precission tool maker, a confectioner, a furniture manufacturer and a wine maker. The bourse could not say when their shares started being traded.
Bursa de Valori Bucuresti now trades 13 of its 16 listed stocks.
Trading on the bourse opens at 0930 local/0730 GMT with a half-hour pre-market pricing session, followed by three and a half hours of continuous trading.
